text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — net.packetloss.high detected in eu-west AZB
oncall-bot: alerts: 45 secs ago. severity: P1. symptoms: transit-provider-z packetloss + sporadic BGP withdraws affecting prefixes used by inference clusters. paging rotation engaged. handoff scheduled +30m.
alex.sre: I'm on it. seeing ~15% packet loss on prefixes 198.51.100.0/24 as seen at our edge facing provider-z. traceroute shows path divergence at provider PE.
alex.sre: quick check: `traceroute -n 198.51.100.1` -> jumps to 203.0.113.254 then drops.
marta.net: confirmed BGP: multiple prefixes flapping; AS path oscillation includes (64500,65000,65002) then back to (64500). neighbor flaps every ~30s. looks like their PE is unstable.
lee.platform: customers are reporting elevated 5xx on eu-west inference endpoints. error-rate spike aligned 10:02–10:08 UTC for many routes. Dedicated customers on eu-west-azb most impacted.
alex.sre: can we stage a temporary reroute via transit-provider-y? need to avoid provider-z until they stabilize.
marta.net: starting prep. plan: advertise specific /24 to provider-y with higher local-pref and no-export to avoid transiting toxic path. applying route-map.
marta.net: ```
bgp neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map RM-TO-Y out
route-map RM-TO-Y permit 10
 set local-preference 200
 set community 65000:100
```
alex.sre: starting packet captures on peering-facing interfaces now:
`tcpdump -i eth-peering 'tcp and host 198.51.100.1' -w /tmp/peering-loss.pcap`
oncall-bot: incident created. pager rotation posted. next handoff assigned to dina-sre.
nate.prodeng: rough customer impact numbers? prometheus shows token error-rate +2% global but +14% eu-west. latency p95 up from 120ms -> 420ms in eu-west.
samir-support: getting support cases: Customer-ID 3247 on Dedicated reporting 504s, support case #8765 opened. Sales notified.
marta.net: peering contact reached; provider-z acknowledges anomalies in their PoP and is investigating. ETA unknown. will request a null-route of the bad internal path.
lee.platform: we can enable multi-region-fallback for heavy customers temporarily. rolling config to prefer eu-central for new sessions. snippet below:
```yaml
routing:
  prefer_region: eu-central
  fallback:
    enabled: true
```
alex.sre: advertising 198.51.100.0/24 to provider-y now via 203.0.113.2 with community 65000:100. monitoring BGP table for path change.
marta.net: advertisement propagated. path selection switched to provider-y for most prefixes. also lowered BFD timers to accelerate detection.
oncall-bot: metric update: packet loss dropped from 15% -> 2% after reroute. DNS SERVFAILs still observed for some resolver replicas in azb-2.
alex.sre: digging into DNS — dig against internal resolver shows intermittent SERVFAILs for our authoritative zone. command run:
`dig +noall +answer @10.0.0.2 inference.redwood.example`
samir-support: preparing status page copy: "We are investigating degraded connectivity to EU region causing elevated latencies and errors for a subset of customers. Engineers are actively rerouting traffic and working with upstream providers." shall I post?
dina-sre: taking over for the next 30m. I'll maintain peering comms and coordinate customer notifications. alex, leave pcaps and bgp logs in /var/tmp/incident-1788887654/
marta.net: peering contact: they will null-route the problematic internal path and perform maintenance on the PE. expected update in ~10m.
lee.platform: after fallback flip, error rates returned to baseline for most customers. a handful pinned to exact eu-west endpoints still impacted (pinned model versions / reserved capacity). samir, can support reach out with instructions to enable failover or temporarily move workload?
samir-support: on it. messaging includes workaround: "switch region or enable failover in Console" + link to runbook.
marta.net: provider update: null-route applied on their edge — our BGP table shows path withdrawn from provider-z. monitoring for stability.
alex.sre: confirm: path stable on provider-y, packet loss <1% now. keeping visibility for 60m. leaving tcpdump capture and bgp snapshots in incident dir.
oncall-bot: update: major degradation mitigated — tickets remain open for follow-up. postmortem assigned to net/peering owners. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/peering-flap :thumbsup:
peering-bot: logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/1788887654/pcap/ and bgp/ .
samir-support: outreach underway to affected customers. closing loop with sales for Dedicated customers.
dina-sre: handing back to marta.net for deep-dive. next steps: collect pcap, BGP RIB snapshots, provider comms, and timeline. assigning postmortem owner: marta.net.
marta.net: noted. will start timeline and include config diffs, AS path graphs, and mitigation timeline. thanks all. :heart:
